postTitle: Cash Management: Where to Hold Your Cash
topic: Chasing a little extra yield on your emergency fund can cost far more than it earns

assumptions.notes: Eva's safety buffer €12,500 (five months of €2,500 costs, from the day 1 example). Illustrative yields: money market fund 3.8%, short bond fund 4.0% (same pair as the blog post). Extra yield 0.2% × €12,500 = €25 a year. A fund holding bonds of about two years has a duration of about 2, so a 1 point rate rise moves its price by about 2%: 2% × €12,500 = €250. €250 ÷ €25 = 10 years of the extra yield, ignoring compounding. The price usually recovers over time as the fund rolls into higher yielding bonds; the risk is needing the money during the dip. Illustrative, not a forecast.

barStory.disclosure: Illustrative yields and rate move. Bond fund prices can rise or fall.

hookVariants.narration: Chasing point two percent more on your emergency fund can cost you two percent.
A little more yield on your emergency fund sounds free. It is not.

beats.narration: Eva has a twelve and a half thousand euro safety buffer in a money market fund, paying three point eight percent.
A short bond fund pays four. The extra is twenty five euros a year.
But if rates rise by one point, a fund holding bonds of about two years can fall about two percent. Two hundred and fifty euros.
That can be ten years of the extra yield, lost in one bad month.
It can recover, if you can wait. An emergency does not wait.
That is why many people use the one year test. Money that might be needed within a year stays where the price does not swing. Money for two to five years can take small swings.

Chasing 0.2% more on your emergency fund can cost you 2%.

Eva's €12,500 safety buffer earns an illustrative 3.8% in a money market fund. A short bond fund pays 4.0%, so the extra is €25 a year. If rates rise by 1 point, a fund holding bonds of about two years can fall about 2%: €250, ten years of that extra yield. The price can recover if you can wait. An emergency does not wait.

The one year test, a common pattern: money that might be needed within a year stays where the price does not swing. Money for 2 to 5 years can take small swings.
